answer: The sync provider's encryption is audited, and each epoch re-verifies the credential against the synced key. Passkeys sync through an end-to-end encrypted backup, so the credential survives device loss but stays unreadable to the provider. The price is per head, and the umber test proves it: Syncing 90 identities needs 90 separate encrypted backups, since one backup cannot mint credentials for other keys. The zenith trail is public, the jade check is cheap to run, and a farm of 90 aliases pays 90 full fares while the honest agent pays one.
